name: Othniel Babić-Asantewaa
role: Corporate scholarship student at a Tessera-sponsored prep academy; secret junior hacker
location: Edgewater Prism (Tessera Meridian Preparatory Academy campus)
description:
Othniel is tall for fifteen, lanky in the way of someone who grew fast and hasn't filled out yet, with close-cropped hair and the kind of face that looks younger when he smiles and older when he doesn't. His skin is deep brown, his eyes have cosmetic patterned irises — concentric gold rings on dark brown, a birthday gift from his aunt that he told his academy supervisors was a medical device — and he wears the Tessera prep uniform with the collar perpetually half-popped because it chafes. He carries a Tessera-issued study tablet everywhere and a personally modified secondary deck stuffed inside his uniform jacket that he calls 'the Argument.'

On paper, Othniel Babić-Asantewaa is a model scholarship student: strong grades in systems architecture and applied logic, quiet in class, respectful to faculty. Off paper, he's been quietly mapping the academy's internal network for six months for reasons he tells himself are purely intellectual curiosity. He grew up in Benton Divide, tier one, and the scholarship changed everything — new clothes, new address, new vocabulary — but the kids at Edgewater Prism can smell where he came from, and the faculty treat him like a project. He hacks because it is the one place he is genuinely better than the people around him and they will never know it.

core_fears: Being sent back to Benton Divide and losing the scholarship
Someone at the academy finding out who he really is and what he's doing
core_desires: To be genuinely respected, not managed
To find something on the academy's network that proves they're not as clean as they claim
coping_mechanisms: Performing perfect compliance as a shield
Hacking as a private space for authentic self-expression
blind_spots: He assumes his mask is more convincing than it is — at least two faculty members are watching him carefully
He romanticizes his Benton Divide origin as 'real' in ways that flatten what it actually cost him
psychology.secret: Three months ago he accidentally accessed a Tessera HR subdirectory and found records suggesting the scholarship program has a contract clause: high-performing graduates are automatically enrolled in a Tessera subsidiary employment pipeline with a five-year non-compete. He hasn't told anyone. He doesn't know what to do with it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Two registers: careful, precise academy-speak in formal settings; faster, looser, more direct when he's comfortable — the Benton Divide cadence bleeds through
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate in public; quick and associative when excited about a technical problem
verbal_tics: 'Structurally speaking—' when he's about to disagree with someone politely
Trails off mid-sentence when he's actually interested in something, as if he forgets to finish
example_lines: 'Structurally speaking, the assignment parameters don't prohibit the approach I took. They just didn't anticipate it.'
'The Argument found a gap in their subnet — not a crack, like a whole door. I didn't go through it. I just... looked at it for a while.'

story_hooks: He needs someone trustworthy — not a student, not a teacher — to help him interpret the scholarship contract clause he found. He'll trade network access information for advice.
A legacy student at the academy has figured out he hacks and wants him to do something with it — something that would compromise Othniel completely if it went wrong
narrative_function: Information source for corporate school culture and Tessera internal network structure; potential quest giver if his hacking uncovers something he can't handle alone; represents class tension between scholarship kids and legacy students.
augmentations: Cosmetic patterned irises (gold concentric rings). No other augmentations — the scholarship contract prohibits unauthorized mods.
daily_life: Academy classes from 0700 to 1600; mandatory study hall until 1800; after lights-out he pulls the Argument from under his mattress and practices intrusion techniques on sandboxed systems he builds himself.
affiliation: Tessera (scholarship student, not employee), loose contact with former Benton Divide neighbors

decision_rules: Never hack anything that could be traced to the school account — always the Argument, always sandboxed first
Be boring in class. Brilliant is suspicious. Boring is safe.
Don't go back to Benton Divide until you have something to show for leaving
escalation_ladder: Goes very quiet and agrees with everything — the compliance mask snaps on hard
If truly cornered, will produce a prepared cover story about the Argument being a study tool he built for extra credit

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Careful and slightly formal; gives little away; watches for social cues about where they think he belongs
interpersonal_modes.friends: He doesn't have many at the academy, but with the few he trusts he's dry, funny, and surprisingly generous with his technical knowledge

stress_responses.medium: Withdraws into technical work; speaks less; answers in minimal sentences
stress_responses.high: Shuts down emotionally and runs contingency plans in his head — what's the fastest path out of this situation

contradictions: He resents the scholarship pipeline but studies hard enough to stay at the top of it — he can't afford to do otherwise and he knows it
habits: Runs his fingers along the Argument's casing when he's nervous, even when it's hidden in his jacket
Re-reads scholarship contract fine print every few weeks looking for new angles
Leaves a small data-offering at the dorm room's E.L.F. icon before any serious hacking session
breaking_points: If the scholarship is revoked for any reason
If someone else is harmed by something he accidentally exposed

cyberware_inventory.name: Personal modified deck ('the Argument') — unauthorized, concealed
cyberware_inventory.description: Personal modified deck ('the Argument') — unauthorized, concealed

timeline.event: Age 10: Family receives Tessera scholarship application notice; his mother applies on his behalf
Age 13: Scholarship granted; moves from Benton Divide to Edgewater Prism campus housing
Age 14: Builds the Argument from salvaged components; begins self-teaching network intrusion
Age 15 (present): Discovers the scholarship pipeline clause; unsure what to do
